plan.estimand: Within-group omnibus effect across 3 time points in one-group repeated-measures design
plan.hypothesis: The repeated-measures ANOVA omnibus null hypothesis: all time-point means are equal

parameters.name: Partial eta-squared (population effect size before correlation adjustment)

assumptions: One-group (single sample) design
Repeated measures at 3 time points
Multivariate normal data
Compound symmetry correlation structure: r = 0.5 between all pairs of time points
No missing data
Univariate F test with sphericity epsilon = 1 (sphericity assumption met)
Omnibus null hypothesis: all time-point means equal
Population effect size: partial eta-squared = 0.08 before correlation adjustment
Effect size f-squared conversion: f² = η²/(1−η²) per G*Power protocol
missing_information: Confirmation of whether the user expects the effect-size calculation to use the standard G*Power formula for repeated-measures ANOVA within-subject effect with correlation structure fully integrated into the noncentrality parameter
clarification_questions: Should the noncentrality parameter incorporate the compound symmetry structure directly (i.e., the effect size adjusted for the correlation = 0.5), or is the partial eta-squared = 0.08 already the effective size after accounting for correlation in the population model?
Is the univariate F test the appropriate choice, or should an alternative (e.g., Wilks Λ multivariate test) be used for power calculation?
scientific_notes: Repeated-measures ANOVA within-subject effect: the noncentrality parameter depends on the correlation structure. With compound symmetry r=0.5 and k=3 time points, the effective variance of the mean difference is reduced relative to independence.
The conversion from partial η² to f (effect size for ANOVA) is: f = √[η²/(1−η²)]. With η² = 0.08, f = √[0.08/0.92] ≈ 0.2946.
Sphericity epsilon = 1 indicates perfect sphericity (equal variances and compound symmetry), so the univariate F test maintains its nominal Type I error rate.
G*Power implements repeated-measures ANOVA sample-size calculation via the noncentral F distribution with df_num = k−1 and df_denom = (n−1)(k−1), where n is the number of participants.
